html:
The order of the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella and Ferdinand, issued at the Alhambra in Granada on 31 March 1492, that all Jews in their kingdoms become Christians or leave by the end of July.

Jews had lived in Spain since Roman times and had flourished in al-Andalus and in the Christian kingdoms. After the massacres of 1391 many converted. The Spanish Inquisition was set up to watch these converts, and the crown claimed that the remaining Jews were drawing them back. Granada had fallen three months before.

Estimates of how many left vary widely, from tens of thousands to well over 100,000; many others converted. Many went first to Portugal, which forced its Jews to convert in 1497, and others to North Africa, Italy and the Ottoman lands. The Ottoman sultan Bayezid II welcomed them, and Thessaloniki and Istanbul became great centres of these Sephardic Jews, who kept their Judeo-Spanish language for centuries. Others later went to Amsterdam and the Americas. Muslims faced the same choice later, ending in the expulsion of the Moriscos. Spain formally revoked the decree in 1968.
sum: The order of the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella and Ferdinand, issued at the Alhambra in Granada on 31 March 1492, that all Jews in their kingdoms become Christians or leave by the end of July.
